November: Into the Dark

November is where dedication separates fair-weather riders from year-round motorcyclists. Days are short, temperatures drop towards winter levels, and rain is frequent. But riding doesn't stop — it just changes character. November riding is about short, purposeful outings rather than epic tours.

Conditions

  • Temperature: Average 5-10°C. Frost becomes regular inland.
  • Daylight: Sunrise around 7:15am, sunset around 4:15pm. Under 9 hours of usable daylight.
  • Weather: Grey, wet, and often windy. November storms can be severe.

November Riding Strategy

  • Plan short rides (50-80 miles) during the warmest, driest part of the day (11am-2pm)
  • Choose routes with shelter — valley roads and forest roads are warmer and less exposed than open moorland
  • Have a destination: a good café, pub lunch, or interesting stop gives the ride purpose beyond just miles
  • Ride with friends — winter rides are more enjoyable and safer in company

Bike Care in November

  • Wash your bike after every ride to remove road salt and grime
  • Apply ACF-50 or similar corrosion protectant to bare metal and electrical connections
  • Keep the chain well-lubricated — wet winter roads strip lube quickly
  • Check tyre pressures weekly — cold reduces air pressure
  • Use a battery tender/trickle charger when the bike is stored

Winter Gear Essentials

November demands proper winter riding gear:

  • Heated grips (ideally heated gloves too)
  • Thermal base layers
  • Waterproof over-suit
  • Pinlock visor insert or anti-fog treatment
  • Insulated waterproof boots
  • High-visibility elements — you need to be seen in dark, grey conditions
November riding is about mindset. Accept that you won't cover big distances or visit mountain passes. Instead, appreciate the raw, elemental nature of riding through autumn's final act. The leafless trees, the low grey skies, and the quiet roads have their own stark beauty.

November Social Riding

November is a good month for social riding events. Fireworks Night (5th November) ride-outs to display locations, Remembrance Day events, and the approach to Christmas all provide riding occasions. Many clubs hold winter socials with indoor events, quiz nights, and planning sessions for the following year.

Use November evenings for route planning and research. Browse OS Maps, read touring blogs, and start planning your 2027 touring calendar. The anticipation of future rides sustains motivation through the darkest months.

Indoor Motorcycle Activities

November is prime time for indoor motorcycle activities. Motorcycle shows begin their winter season, with Motorcycle Live at the NEC typically falling in late November. Local clubs hold their winter social programmes — quiz nights, film evenings, and planning sessions for the following year. Some dealers host open evenings with new model previews and pizza nights that keep the motorcycle community connected through the dark months.

If you're mechanically inclined, November evenings are ideal for workshop projects — fitting accessories, performing maintenance, or even beginning a winter restoration project. The satisfaction of working on your bike feeds the same passion as riding it, and the results are ready for spring.
keyTakeaways: November averages 5-10C with regular inland frost, and grey, wet, windy weather is common.
Daylight drops under 9 hours, with sunrise around 7:15am and sunset around 4:15pm.
The strategy is short, purposeful rides of 50-80 miles during the warmest hours, 11am to 2pm.
Choose sheltered valley and forest roads with a good cafe or pub as a destination.
Wash the bike after every ride and apply ACF-50 to protect against corrosive road salt.

faq.q: Can you still ride a motorcycle in November?
faq.a: Yes, but November riding changes character. Days are short, temperatures drop towards winter levels and rain is frequent, so it is about short, purposeful outings rather than epic tours. Plan rides of 50 to 80 miles during the warmest, driest part of the day, roughly 11am to 2pm, and choose routes with a good cafe or pub as a destination.

faq.q: What gear do I need for November?
faq.a: November demands proper winter gear: heated grips and ideally heated gloves, thermal base layers, a waterproof over-suit, a Pinlock visor insert or anti-fog treatment, and insulated waterproof boots. High-visibility elements are important because you need to be seen in dark, grey conditions. Sheltered valley and forest roads are warmer and less exposed than open moorland.

faq.q: How do I protect my bike in November?
faq.a: Wash your bike after every ride to remove road salt and grime, and apply ACF-50 or a similar corrosion protectant to bare metal and electrical connections. Keep the chain well lubricated because wet, gritty winter roads strip lube quickly, check tyre pressures weekly as cold reduces air pressure, and use a battery tender when the bike is stored.

faq.q: Are there riding events in November?
faq.a: November is a good month for social riding. Fireworks Night ride-outs on the 5th, Remembrance Day events and the approach to Christmas all provide occasions to ride. Motorcycle Live at the NEC typically falls in late November, and many clubs run winter social programmes with quiz nights, film evenings and planning sessions for the following year.

faq.q: What can I do on the bike when it is too wet to ride?
faq.a: Use November evenings for route planning and research, browsing OS Maps, reading touring blogs and building your touring calendar for the following year. If you are mechanically inclined, the dark evenings are ideal for workshop projects such as fitting accessories, performing maintenance or beginning a winter restoration, so the bike is ready the moment spring arrives.
